paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole stretch of Moses' speech is saying: God cares about the people who get squeezed. The poor man needs his cloak to sleep in, so give it back by sunset (Deuteronomy 24:12-13). The hired hand needs his pay today, because he depends on it (Deuteronomy 24:15). The foreigner, the fatherless and the widow get what's left in the field (Deuteronomy 24:19-21).

And look at the reason Moses keeps giving: "Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from that place." (Deuteronomy 24:18) Israel didn't earn their freedom. They were handed mercy, so now they hand it on. I know a little about being pulled out of a dark place I couldn't escape on my own, and let me tell you, it changes how you treat the next person in the dark. Your kindness is the thank-you note, friend, and God reads every one.

It's the same thread in the courtroom and the marketplace. A guilty man gets his lashes, but no more than forty, so that he isn't degraded (Deuteronomy 25:3). An honest scale matters because everyone who cheats with weights is "detestable to the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 25:16). So here's your batch to carry out the door: treat people fairly, treat the weak gently, and never forget who rescued you first. Moses isn't done yet, so stick around!
